trackers.name: Apple Watch

capability_notes.heart_rate: Periodic heart rate is sent from Apple Watch to Health automatically.
capability_notes.hrv: HealthKit records SDNN samples on Apple Watch automatically. Series 12 and Ultra 4 also show Recovery HRV on the watch.
capability_notes.resting_hr: Estimated by the system from sedentary heart rate. Apple Watch may replace the current or previous day's sample with a better estimate.
capability_notes.sleep_stages: Awake, REM, Core and Deep when Track Sleep with Apple Watch is on.
capability_notes.respiratory_rate: Recorded during sleep. Not available for users under 13.
capability_notes.spo2: Series 6 or later and all Ultra models; not SE. US watches bought on or after 18 Jan 2024 (part numbers LW/A, LS/A) are analysed on iPhone, and results still appear in Health.

setup_steps: On iPhone, open Health → Summary → your picture → Devices → your Apple Watch → Privacy Settings, and turn on Fitness Tracking.
In Health → Browse → Sleep, set a sleep schedule and turn on Track Sleep with Apple Watch.
habits: Wear your Apple Watch to bed. Sleep stages, breathing rate and overnight blood oxygen need it.
Charge it before bedtime. Turn on Charging Reminders in Watch → My Watch → Sleep.
limits: Blood oxygen needs Apple Watch Series 6 or later or any Ultra. It isn't available on Apple Watch SE.
Breathing rate isn't available for users under 13.

trackers.name: Garmin

capability_notes.heart_rate: All-day heart rate. Timed activities send only high and low values.
capability_notes.hrv: Not in Garmin's list of data Apple Health receives. HRV stays in Garmin Connect.
capability_notes.resting_hr: Not in Garmin's list. Garmin sends Resting Energy, not resting heart rate.
capability_notes.sleep_stages: Garmin doesn't say. Third-party reports say stages are sent since Garmin Connect 4.71 (Sept 2023).
capability_notes.workouts: Activities uploaded to Garmin Connect. GPS tracks aren't sent.

setup_steps: Open Garmin Connect → More → Settings → Connect Apps.
Under Available Apps, tap Apple Health → Connect with Apple Health.
Turn on all data types, then tap Allow.
To check later: open Health → Summary → your picture → Apps → Connect → Turn On All.
habits: Open Garmin Connect each morning and keep it on screen until it has synced. It sends data to Apple Health only while it's open in the foreground.
Sync your watch first. Garmin Connect passes data to Apple Health after each successful watch sync.
limits: Garmin Connect doesn't send HRV, resting heart rate, breathing rate or blood oxygen to Apple Health.
Workout heart rate arrives as high and low values only, and GPS tracks aren't sent.
Connect doesn't appear in Apple Health if only an Edge bike computer is registered to your Garmin account.

sources.covers: Data types sent, foreground requirement, setup in both apps, source name 'Connect'

trackers.name: Oura

capability_notes.hrv: Not in Oura's list of data exported to Apple Health.
capability_notes.sleep_stages: Oura exports sleep duration, start, end and stages.
capability_notes.respiratory_rate: Average nighttime respiratory rate (one value per night).
capability_notes.workouts: Manually added, recorded with Activity Heart Rate, or from Automatic Activity Detection.

setup_steps: Open Oura → menu (top left) → Settings.
Under Data sharing, tap Apple Health.
Turn on Connect to Health and allow all data types.
To check later: open Health → Summary → your picture → Apps → Oura → Turn On All.
habits: Open Oura every morning. Your data reaches Apple Health only after Oura is opened.
Keep Background App Refresh on for Oura and Low Power Mode off.
limits: Oura doesn't send HRV, resting heart rate or blood oxygen to Apple Health.
Breathing rate arrives as one nightly average.
On Gen3 and later rings, Apple Health sync needs an active Oura membership.

sources.covers: Export list, setup, membership requirement, Background App Refresh and Low Power Mode (last updated 2026-10-14)

trackers.name: Polar

capability_notes.heart_rate: Heart rate during workouts only. Polar: 'Continuous heart rate is not synced.'
capability_notes.hrv: Not in Polar's list of synced data.
capability_notes.sleep: Sleep duration, time of falling asleep and time of waking up.
capability_notes.sleep_stages: Polar lists duration and times only.
capability_notes.workouts: Type, duration, distance, start, end, total active energy and average heart rate.

setup_steps: Open Polar Flow → More → General settings.
Turn on Apple Health.
Tap Turn All Categories On, then Allow.
To check later: open Health → Summary → your picture → Apps → Polar Flow → Turn On All.
habits: Sync your watch with Polar Flow. New data then goes to Apple Health.
Data missing? In Polar Flow → More → General settings, tap Sync now. It resends the last two weeks.
limits: Polar Flow sends heart rate for workouts only, with no all-day heart rate.
Polar Flow doesn't send HRV, resting heart rate, sleep stages, breathing rate or blood oxygen.

sources.covers: Synced data list, setup, Sync now, priority

trackers.name: Suunto

capability_notes.heart_rate: Suunto publishes no data-type list. Users on Suunto's forum report heart rate, steps and workouts arriving.
capability_notes.hrv: Users on Suunto's forum report no HRV in Apple Health.
capability_notes.sleep: Users on Suunto's forum report no sleep permission or sleep data in Apple Health.
capability_notes.workouts: Users report workouts arriving without GPS tracks.

setup_steps: Open the Suunto app and go to its settings to start sharing with Apple Health.
Allow all data types when iOS asks.
To check later: open Health → Summary → your picture → Apps → Suunto → Turn On All.
limits: Suunto doesn't publish what its app sends to Apple Health. Check sync shows what arrives.

trackers.name: COROS

capability_notes.heart_rate: Listed by COROS. Another COROS article says daily data isn't supported for third-party export, so all-day heart rate is unconfirmed.
capability_notes.hrv: Not in COROS's list of supported Apple Health data types.
capability_notes.sleep_stages: COROS doesn't say whether stages are included.
capability_notes.workouts: COROS release notes: activities synced to Apple Health distinguish indoor/outdoor running and cycling, and pool/open-water swims.

setup_steps: Open COROS → Profile → Settings → 3rd Party Apps → Data Sync → Apple Health.
Select all data types to sync.
To check later: open Health → Summary → your picture → Apps → COROS and turn on all types.
habits: Sync your watch with the COROS app on a stable internet connection. Workouts go to Apple Health when the watch syncs.
limits: COROS doesn't send HRV, resting heart rate, breathing rate or blood oxygen to Apple Health.

trackers.name: Withings

capability_notes.heart_rate: Listed as shareable. Withings states that sleep-mat heart rate (Sleep, Sleep Analyzer) doesn't sync to Apple Health.
capability_notes.hrv: Heart Rate Variability is in Withings' list of categories 'shared between the apps', with no direction given.
capability_notes.resting_hr: In the shared-categories list, with no direction given.
capability_notes.sleep: In the shared-categories list, with no direction given.
capability_notes.respiratory_rate: In the shared-categories list, with no direction given.
capability_notes.spo2: Blood Oxygen is in the shared-categories list, with no direction given.
capability_notes.workouts: In the shared-categories list, with no direction given.
capability_notes.steps: In the shared-categories list, with no direction given.

setup_steps: Open Withings → Profile → Settings (gear) → Export health data to Apple Health.
Tap Next twice, turn on all data types, then tap Allow and Done.
To check later: open Health → Summary → your picture → Apps → Withings → Turn On All.
habits: Withings doesn't sync to Apple Health automatically. Open Withings, then the Health app, then pull down on the Withings Home tab to refresh.
Allow up to 15 minutes after a measurement.
limits: Accounts created on or after 13 October 2026 need a Withings+ subscription to send data to Apple Health.
Heart rate from the under-mattress sleep sensor doesn't reach Apple Health.

trackers.name: Fitbit

capability_notes.hrv: Google Health reads HRV from Apple Health but doesn't write it.
capability_notes.workouts: Google lists Exercise and Exercise routes.
capability_notes.sleep_stages: Google lists Sleep session and Sleep stages.

setup_steps: Sign in to Google Health with an adult Google Account.
Open Google Health → Connections (top left) → Apps and services.
Under Add connections, tap Apple Health → Get started → Agree.
Tap Turn All Categories On, then Allow, then Done.
habits: Keep Google Health up to date.
If Google Health shows 'New data types available', review and grant them.
limits: Google Health doesn't send HRV to Apple Health.
Needs iOS 16.4 or later and an adult Google Account.

trackers.name: Just my iPhone

capability_notes.heart_rate: iPhone has no heart sensor. AirPods Pro 3 add heart rate during workouts.
capability_notes.sleep: With a sleep schedule set, iPhone estimates time in bed. There are no stages.
capability_notes.workouts: Workouts started in the Fitness app's Workout tab on iPhone.
capability_notes.steps: Steps, flights climbed, walking distance and mobility metrics from iPhone's sensors.

setup_steps: Open Settings → Privacy & Security → Motion & Fitness and turn on Fitness Tracking.
In Health → Browse → Sleep, set a sleep schedule.
habits: Carry your iPhone during the day. It counts steps with its own sensors.
limits: Without a wearable, iPhone records no heart rate, HRV, resting heart rate, sleep stages, breathing rate or blood oxygen.
Sleep is an estimate of time in bed from your sleep schedule.
Heart rate arrives only during workouts with AirPods Pro 3.
